newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay to close Hallein plant in Austria.
newsitem.headline: Solvay to close Hallein plant in Austria.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA said in a statement on Wednesday it would close down its electrolytic unit at Hallein, near Salzburg, in Austria by the end of the year.
The plant makes caustic soda, liquid chlorine and chlorine derivatives.
"Despite long negotiations with its suppliers, there is no perspective for the Hallein plant to regain profitability in the foreseeable future," Solvay said in a statement.
It said that even if efforts to increase productivity had been successful, the Hallein plant had been making considerable losses for several years.

The plant had suffered a cash drain due to the high cost of industrial salt, bought from Austrian salt mines, as well as the higher-than-average cost of electricity in Austria. The plant was too small to be competitive, it said.
Solvay employs 90 people at the Hallein plant.

"For the people involved a social scheme will be discussed with the representative organisations, whilst a limited number of employees will be maintained to operate a storage facility," the statement added.
The Solvay group is based in 44 countries, generating annual sales of 273 billion Belgian francs from its five sectors of activity, which are alkalis, peroxygens, plastics, processing and healthcare.
